name: Logit processing and token sampling
arithmetic_intensity: Also memory-bound and batch-invariant in the worst way. Reading the final logits for a vocab V from HBM costs 2*V bytes per token at bf16 (a single fp32 row is 4*V), and the softmax/top-k/renormalize arithmetic is a few multiples of V - so AI is on the order of 1-2 flop/byte and, critically, is essentially INDEPENDENT of batch: every sequence in the batch pays its own 2*V bytes even though the sampler is one kernel. The catch-all cost is the last hidden state (2*hidden_width bytes) and, on large-vocab models, the LM head weight matrix (2*hidden_width*V bytes) - the LM head is itself a GEMM over vocab-sized output and for big vocabs is a second full decode GEMM. For Llama-2-class vocab 32k and hidden 4096, the logits alone are ~256 KB per token at fp32.
scales_with: vocab_size (logit bytes per token scale linearly with V)
batch_size (logit bytes scale linearly with B - sampling gets no batching benefit per token)
num_sampled_candidates (multiple-return sampling multiplies the softmax work)
temperature_and_top_p (compute cost of the sort/partial-sort, not memory)

vocab-to-param ratio V/P (the crossover test for DEVICE-side sampling being visible at all: 2*V/P of the step's bytes = 0.0032% for Llama-3-8B, 0.00095% for a Llama-2-7B-class vocab, ~5% only for a sub-1B model with a 128k vocab)

host-vs-device placement (this decides the regime: device-side sampling is 4*V bytes/token and negligible for every modern dense model, host-side sampling moves the same 4*V bytes to the CPU plus a serialised O(n_vocab) walk and becomes a batch-driven bottleneck - see host-side-sampling-loop)
logits dtype at the sampler (vLLM casts the whole [B, V] tensor to fp32 every step regardless of the model's output dtype, doubling both the device traffic and any downstream host payload)
workarounds: Fused sampling kernels (top-k / top-p / Gumbel) that read the logits once from HBM and do selection in registers
FlashInfer-style JIT-sampled sampling to avoid materializing the full V-wide distribution
LM-head quantization, or keeping the LM head in a lower precision, since it is a bandwidth cost like any other decode GEMM
Speculative sampling's rejection scheme, which replaces sampling from a V-wide distribution with a V-wide comparison against draft tokens
Batched sampling that coalesces many sequences' logits into one memory transaction
Keep the logits tensor in 2-byte form through the sampling chain unless fp32 is required, since the fp32 cast doubles the V-wide traffic on both device and host
notes: Design consequence: sampling is small in flops and embarrassingly memory-bound, so its cost shows up as inter-token latency variance - a latency spike at the end of every step. Sampling cost per token is roughly fixed regardless of batch, so at high batch it becomes a small share of step time; at batch 1 it is a real share of it. Engine authors should fuse it rather than splitting softmax, top-k and multinomial draw into separate kernels, each of which re-reads the same V-wide vector. Hardware: nothing here stresses tensor cores; a part with modest FLOPS and high bandwidth serves sampling perfectly well, and on very large-vocab models the LM head deserves to be budgeted as a decode GEMM rather than as 'just sampling'. CROSSOVER / WHERE IT STARTS TO MATTER, deepened 2026-10-03: the record above gives the byte count but not the regime test, so here is the arithmetic. Sampling's device cost is 4*V bytes per token at fp32 (2*V at bf16) against a decode step that streams 2*P bytes of weights, i.e. sampling is 4*V/(2*P) = 2*V/P of the step's bytes. Llama-3-8B: 2*128256/8.03e9 = 0.0032%. Llama-2-7B-class with V=32000, P=6.74e9: 0.00095%. A small model with a large vocab is the worst case in the family and still only ~1% - e.g. a 0.5B model with a 128k vocab gives 2*128256/0.5e9 = 5.1%, which is the only shape in which plain sampling becomes a visible share of a DEVICE-bound step. The practical crossovers therefore are not about vocab: (i) device-side sampling crosses from negligible to visible only for models with V/P > ~0.01, i.e. sub-1B with a large vocab; (ii) HOST-side sampling crosses at batch ~32 and is governed by n_vocab x batch x 4 B moved to the CPU - see host-side-sampling-loop, where the measured D2H per copy goes 608.3 KB at 1 slot to 16,157.4 KB at 32 slots and removing the transfer is worth 48% throughput; (iii) sampling becomes a KERNEL-count problem the moment the step is launch-overhead-bound, because min_p alone is four to five full-width passes plus a chain of separately registered ops. One implementation detail that quietly doubles the cost: vLLM's sampler does an unconditional logits.to(torch.float32) every step, so even a bf16 model writes and re-reads the V-wide tensor at 4 bytes/element on the sampling path.
